thread:
oncall-bot: ALERT: apac1 ingress: 5xx spike (502/503) and increased TLS handshake resets detected. Traffic impact ~12% across apac1 AZB/AZC. Auto-escalation -> on-call. https://grafana.redwood/influx/apac1/ingress/errors

alice: I'm on it. grabbing graphs and checking health checks now. assigning to self.

ben: seeing ConnectionErrorCount and BackendResponseTime jump on ALB in apac1b around 09:47 UTC. also TLS handshake failures reported by our envoy fleet (RST_STREAM, code=2).

carla: copying tcpdump from one of the failing envoy pods:```09:47:12.345 IP loadbalancer.443 > backend.32456: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0```looks like LB is sending RST to backend during TLS handshake.

ben: ALB target-health shows many targets UNHEALTHY in apac1b. TargetGroup TG-ingress-apac1b has increasing 504/502.

alice: rolling through runbook: 1) check ALB access logs 2) check envoy pod logs 3) verify NLB passthrough settings 4) consider draining AZ if isolated. anyone else seeing networking noise?

dino: yes, VPC flow logs show drops between ALB ENI and node ENI in apac1b starting at 09:46:30. Looks like upstream hypervisor networking issues on that AZ.

carla: quick envoy log snippet:```[2026-03-15T09:47:14Z] envoy [warning] TLS error: handshake failed: remote error: tls: internal error; stream reset (RST_STREAM)```

alice: ok this matches. plan: fail traffic away from apac1b to apac1a/c and increase NLB idle timeout to avoid mid-handshake closes. prepping commands now.

ben: running a staged target deregister for TG-ingress-apac1b (30s drain). command:
```aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --targets Id=i-0abc123 --region apac1```

carla: also bumping keepalive in our envoy configmap to 120s to match LB idle. patching with kubectl:```kubectl -n ingress patch configmap envoy-cm -p '{"data":{"tcp_keepalive":"120"}}'```

oncall-bot: NOTE: automated failover rules triggered a route shift for 6% of traffic to euc1 as fallback while drain proceeds.

dino: we should also reduce Route53 TTL for apac1 endpoints to 30s to let client re-resolve quicker if we need to shift more. doing `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch ...` now.

ben: ALB connection errors dropping after target deregister and keepalive bump. 5xx rate down from 12% -> 3% in last 3m.

alice: monitoring for recurrence. creating incident ticket and noting customer impact: several production customers hit increased errors, major user-facing pages degraded for ~11m window.

carla: flagging merchant-account and billing teams, two high-traffic customers showed 50-80% errors during spike. logged in support ticket #INC-31415.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: escalation acknowledged. on-call handoff scheduled in 45 minutes.

dino: quick postmortem notes: probable AZ-level networking hardware flaps between ALB ENIs and instances, causing mid-TLS handshake RSTs. mitigations applied: drained apac1b targets, bumped keepalive, Route53 TTL lowered, fallback routing to euc1.

alice: status update to customers drafted and posted to status.redwood: "We experienced elevated 5xx errors in APAC region due to ingress load-balancer networking failures. Traffic rerouted, mitigations applied, errors reduced. Engineers are investigating root cause with cloud provider."

sre-bot: REMINDER: collect perf snapshots and attach to ticket. run:```/usr/local/bin/collect-infra-snapshot --region apac1 --since 2026-03-15T09:45:00Z```

ben: attaching ALB access log excerpt:```"2026-03-15T09:47:13Z elb 10.0.0.1:443 10.0.0.10:32456 502 502 0 123 0 0 "TLS handshake error"```

carla: handing off to morning oncall @dino for follow-ups and provider escalation. leaving runbook state and commands in the ticket.

dino: thanks, taking over. immediate next steps: engage cloud provider support for ENI/hypervisor checks, ensure no further target flaps, verify quotas. will update every 30m or on key findings.

alice: thanks all — saving logs and timeline. will join postmortem later.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations reduced user-facing errors to <1% for apac1 as of 09:56 UTC. monitoring until 10:30 UTC.

carla: created post-incident board at https://confluence.redwood/incident/2099502468. notes/timeline/commands attached.

alice: summary for handoff to ops: root hypothesis = AZ network hardware/hypervisor causing RSTs mid-TLS, impact ~12% traffic, duration ~11m, mitigations = target drain, keepalive bump, TTL reduce, fallback routing. action items: provider escalation, ALB health-check tuning, consider sticky healthcheck circuit for single-AZ flaps.

dino: acknowledged. will update ticket and escalate. closing Slack thread for now; reopen if error rate rises. :thumbsup:
